newsitem.title: USA: American dentist extradited from New Zealand.
newsitem.headline: American dentist extradited from New Zealand.

text.p: An orthodonist who fled the country 11 years ago rather than face pedophilia charges was extradited to New York on Tuesday from New Zealand, officials said.
Kenneth D'Cunha, 40, was accused in 1986 of participating in a pedophile and pornography ring that allegedly lured teenage boys to sex parties with offers of drugs and alcohol.

He was indicted in June 1986 on eight counts of sodomy and was to have turned himself in to authorities on July 9, 1986. Instead he fled, and avoided capture until he was arrested in New Plymouth, New Zealand, in January on an Interpol warrant.

The dentist, who had a practice in Danbury, Connecticut, was indicted with five other men, including a Boy Scout leader and a school teacher. His co-defendants received sentences ranging from five years probation to nine years in prison.
D'Cunha faces up to seven years in prison, if convicted. He pleaded not guilty at an arraignment on Tuesday and was ordered back in court on July 17 for a bail hearing.
He was planning to open a dental proactice in New Zealand, authorities said.

In 1987, police tracked D'Cunha to Canada where extradition proceedings were underway when he disappeared again. Four years later, he turned up in Melbourne, Australia, where he phoned Philip Sanford, an orthodontist in New Zealand, saying he wanted to work for him, according to court papers filed in New Zealand.
D'Cunha worked for Sanford from November 1995 to March 1996, when D'Cunha sued Sanford for wrongful dismissal.
His arrest came a few months later when Sanford mentioned the lawsuit to a U.S. colleague who recognised D'Cunha's name from publicity about the case, a source said.
